welcome.title: Welcome to your Traflinq trial
welcome.bodyPool: You have 72 hours to explore pool car management and chauffeur bookings.
welcome.bodyShuttle: You have 72 hours to explore shuttle routes and employee commute.
welcome.bodyBoth: You have 72 hours to explore pool chauffeur and shuttle commute. We'll guide you through both modules.

sectionPool.title: Part 1 — Pool (chauffeur)
sectionPool.body: Start with pool fleet and bookings.

sectionShuttle.title: Part 2 — Shuttle
sectionShuttle.body: Now set up shuttle fleet, routes, and employee assignments.

poolWelcome.title: Pool trial — chauffeur bookings
poolWelcome.body: Add a vehicle and chauffeur driver to your fleet, then assign them when you create a booking.

poolVehicle.title: Add a fleet vehicle
poolVehicle.body: Register a company vehicle in Fleet. Assign it when creating a self-managed chauffeur booking.

poolDriver.title: Invite a chauffeur driver
poolDriver.body: Add a chauffeur-type driver to your fleet for bookings.

poolBooking.title: Create a booking
poolBooking.body: Create a self-managed chauffeur booking using your pool vehicle and driver. Add employees first if you need passengers other than yourself.

shuttleWelcome.title: Shuttle trial — routes & employees
shuttleWelcome.body: Use your company fleet: add a vehicle and shuttle driver, then assign them when you create a route.

shuttleVehicle.title: Add a fleet vehicle
shuttleVehicle.body: Register a company vehicle with seat capacity. You will assign it to a shuttle route later.

shuttleDriver.title: Invite a shuttle driver
shuttleDriver.body: Add a shuttle-type driver to your fleet. They use these credentials in the driver mobile app.

shuttleRoute.title: Create a route
shuttleRoute.body: Build a route with at least two stops and assign your shuttle vehicle and driver.

shuttleEmployees.title: Add & assign employees
shuttleEmployees.body: Create up to 3 employees (6 if you selected both modules), then assign them to your route from the Routes page.

shuttleTest.title: Generate trips & test
shuttleTest.body: Open your route to track trips. Generate scheduled trips for today, then test with the driver and employee apps.

app.title: Mobile apps
app.body: Drivers use the chauffeur/shuttle driver app with credentials from the invite step. Employees use the employee app with credentials shown when you create each employee.

merge.identified: {routeA} has {assignedA} assigned employees for {seatsA} seats ({pctA}%) and {routeB} has {assignedB} for {seatsB} seats ({pctB}%). They serve nearby areas and the same office.
merge.recommendation: Run {routeB} together with {routeA} on {keptVehicle} and stop using {removedVehicle} on this route.
merge.why: Fixed cost eliminated: {fixed} per month. The longer merged route adds {added} of fuel per month. Estimated net saving after the extra fuel: {net} per month.

tradeoff.distance: {vehicle} drives {km} km more per day and uses about {litres} L more fuel.
tradeoff.time: The kept vehicle's route gets about {minutes} minutes longer per day.
tradeoff.vendor_fuel: {vehicle}'s vendor rate includes fuel, so the extra fuel is the vendor's cost — the vendor may ask to reprice.

reseq.identified: {route} ({direction}) visits its stops in an order that drives {km} km; the same stops can be covered in {optimizedKm} km.
reseq.recommendation: Change the stop order of {route} ({direction}) to the optimized sequence shown on the map.
reseq.why: It removes {km} km per trip while keeping every pickup, saving about {net} of fuel per month.

tradeoff.ride: Passengers at {stop} ride about {minutes} min longer.

downsize.identified: {vehicle} has {seats} seats, but no route it serves has more than {assigned} assigned employees ({pct}%).
downsize.why: The smaller vehicle still seats every assigned employee and costs about {net} less per month (rent and fuel).

tradeoff.headroom: Only {spare} spare seats remain for new employees on these routes.

detour.identified: {trips} of {total} {direction} trips on {route} drove more than 1.2× the planned distance — {km} extra km in total.
detour.recommendation: Review these trips with the driver and vendor and keep the vehicle on the planned route.
detour.why: At this rate the extra distance costs about {net} of fuel per month.

fuel.identified: {vehicle} drove {km} km (GPS). At its rated {kmpl} km/L that is about {estimated} L, but the vendor's claimed fuel for the period is {contracted} L — {diff} L ({pct}%) more.
fuel.recommendation: Ask the vendor to bill {vehicle}'s fuel for the distance it actually drives.
fuel.why: At the recorded fuel price the vendor's claimed fuel costs {amount} more for the period than the fuel the distance driven needs.

redistribute.identified: {route} carries {assigned} assigned employees in {seats} seats ({pct}%), while {receivers} other routes to the same office have {freeSeats} free seats.
redistribute.recommendation: Move {route}'s employees to {receivers} and stop using {vehicle}.
redistribute.why: Removing the vehicle saves its fixed cost of {fixed} per month. The receiving routes burn {added} more fuel per month. After that extra fuel, the estimated net saving is {net} per month.
redistribute.recommendation_rejected: {route}'s employees cannot all be moved to other routes within the limits.
redistribute.why_rejected: {stops} pickup stop(s) are too far from any route with free seats.

tradeoff.distance: {receivers} drive {km} km more per day in total.
tradeoff.headroom: The fullest receiving route is left with {spare} free seat(s) for new employees.
